14: # Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines
15: 
16: Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### When to Create Assets
21: 
22: **Create an asset file when:**
23: - Templates users apply repeatedly
24: - Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
25: - Multiple examples of same pattern exist
26: - Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
27: - Template variations for different scenarios
28: 
29: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
30: - Content <30 lines
31: - Tightly coupled to workflow logic
32: - Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
33: - Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)
34: 
35: ### Location & Naming
36: 
37: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`
38: 
39: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension
40: 
41: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
42: |---------------|-----------------|
43: | `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
44: | `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
45: | `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
46: | `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES
51: 
52: ### Template Files
53: **Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks
54: 
55: **Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
56: - Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`
57: 
58: **Structure**:
59: - One template per section
60: - Include field descriptions
61: - Show complete examples
62: - Explain when to use each template
63: 
64: **Use cases**:
65: - Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
66: - Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
67: - Code templates (functions, classes, modules)
68: 
69: ### Reference Files
70: **Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data
71: 
72: **Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
73: - Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`
74: 
75: **Structure**:
76: - Tables or lists for quick lookup
77: - Decision matrices
78: - Classification systems
79: - Standards and conventions
80: 
81: **Use cases**:
82: - Emoji selection guides
83: - File type classifications
84: - Validation rule sets
85: - Naming conventions
86: 
87: ### Example Files
88: **Purpose**: Show working examples of skill outputs
89: 
90: **Naming**: `[topic]-examples.md`
91: - Example: `optimization-examples.md`, `skill-examples.md`
92: 
93: **Structure**:
94: - Before/after comparisons
95: - Annotated examples
96: - Multiple variations
97: - Anti-patterns to avoid
98: 
99: **Use cases**:
100: - Complete skill applications
101: - Common patterns
102: - Edge cases
103: - Quality standards
104: 
105: ### Guide Files
106: **Purpose**: Detailed how-to guides for complex processes
107: 
108: **Naming**: `[process]-guide.md`
109: - Example: `packaging-guide.md`, `distribution-guide.md`
110: 
111: **Structure**:
112: - Step-by-step instructions
113: - Troubleshooting sections
114: - Best practices
115: - Common pitfalls
116: 
117: **Use cases**:
118: - Multi-step processes
119: - Advanced techniques
120: - Workflow deep-dives
121: - Integration guides
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
126: 
127: ### Title and Intro
128: 
129: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
130: 
131: ```markdown
132: ---
133: title: [Title]
134: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
135: trigger_phrases:
136:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
137:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
138:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
139: importance_tier: normal
140: contextType: general
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: 
144: # [Title]
145: 
146: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
147: 
148: \## 1. OVERVIEW
149: 
150: ### Purpose
151: 
152: [Why this asset exists]
153: 
154: ### Usage
155: 
156: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: \## 2. [Content Section]
161: 
162: [The actual template/checklist/snippet content]
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## N. Related Resources (optional, if present must be last)
167: 
168: [Links to related files]
169: 
170: ```
171: 
172: Every asset file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content, `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, and `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
173: 
174: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and OVERVIEW section.**
175: > The intro is a hook. OVERVIEW provides the details.
176: 
177: #### GOOD Intro Structure
178: 
179: ```markdown
180: # Git Commit Templates
181: 
182: Copy the template that matches the change, fill the fields, and commit.
183: 
184: \## 1. OVERVIEW
185: 
186: ### Purpose
187: 
188: Uniform messages let a reader scan history by intent instead of by author.
189: 
190: ### Usage
191: 
192: Copy the appropriate template based on commit type...
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: \## 2. COMMIT TEMPLATES
197: ...
198: ```
199: 
200: #### BAD Intro Structure (too long, has subsections)
201: 
202: ```markdown
203: # Git Commit Templates
204: 
205: Copy-paste templates for creating well-structured commit messages.
206: 
207: ### Core Principle    ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
208: Atomic commits with clear intent = maintainable history.
209: 
210: ### When to Use       ← WRONG: This belongs in OVERVIEW section!
211: - Creating new features
212: - Fixing bugs
213: 
214: ---
215: ```
216: 
217: ### Intro vs OVERVIEW Content Placement
218: 
219: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | OVERVIEW Section       |
220: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
221: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat)    |
222: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
223: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
224: | How to copy/customize | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
225: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
226: | Any H2/H3 subsections | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES                  |
227:

305: ## 5. LOGIC REPRESENTATION PATTERNS
306: 
307: **Purpose**: Guidelines for representing logic, workflows, and decision trees in asset files using structured formats instead of prose.
308: 
309: **Why Structured Logic?**
310: - **Clarity**: Executable-style logic is easier to understand than prose
311: - **AI-Friendly**: LLMs parse structured logic better than narrative descriptions
312: - **Maintainability**: Changes to logic are more visible in structured formats
313: - **Consistency**: Same patterns across all asset files
314: 
315: ### When to Use Each Format
316: 
317: **Use Python Pseudo-Code When:**
318: - Complex branching logic (multiple IF/ELIF/ELSE conditions)
319: - Function/method definitions with clear inputs/outputs
320: - State management or algorithmic processes
321: - Validation or transformation logic
322: - Examples: Mode detection, validation pipelines, decision functions
323: 
324: **Use YAML Structures When:**
325: - Configuration data (settings, options, parameters)
326: - Pipeline definitions (multi-step workflows with clear phases)
327: - Hierarchical workflows (nested processes)
328: - Metadata structures (categorization, tagging)
329: - Examples: Workflow definitions, configuration templates, feature matrices
330: 
331: **Use Markdown Decision Trees When:**
332: - Simple branching logic (2-5 branches)
333: - Visual flow representation (user-facing paths)
334: - Classification systems (type determination)
335: - Quick decision guides
336: - Examples: Document type selection, frontmatter requirements
337: 
338: **Keep Markdown Prose When:**
339: - Explanatory text and conceptual overviews
340: - Narrative examples with context
341: - Best practices guidance
342: - Introductions and summaries
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## 6. DECISION LOGIC EXAMPLES
347: 
348: **Purpose**: Demonstrate how to convert markdown prose into structured decision logic.
349: 
350: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Mode Detection
351: 
352: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
353: ```markdown
354: Check user input for mode indicators:
355: - If "$quick" is present, use quick mode with auto-scaling depth
356: - If "$ticket" is present, use ticket mode with depth 10
357: - Otherwise, use interactive mode with depth 10
358: ```
359: 
360: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
361: ```python
362: def detect_mode(request):
363:     """Detect execution mode from user request markers"""
364: 
365:     if '$quick' in request:
366:         mode = 'quick'
367:         depth = 'auto_scale_1_to_5'
368:     elif '$ticket' in request:
369:         mode = 'ticket'
370:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
371:     else:
372:         # DEFAULT TO INTERACTIVE
373:         mode = 'interactive'
374:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
375: 
376:     return mode, depth
377: ```
378: 
379: ### Markdown Decision Tree: Frontmatter Requirements
380: 
381: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
382: ```markdown
383: Different document types have different frontmatter requirements:
384: - SKILL.md files must have frontmatter with name, description, allowed-tools, and version
385: - Command files must have frontmatter with description and argument-hint
386: - Skill reference/asset files must have the 5-field block
387: - Knowledge files outside skill folders should not have frontmatter
388: - Spec files typically don't have frontmatter
389: ```
390: 
391: **After (Markdown Decision Tree)**:
392: ```
393: Document type?
394: ├─> SKILL.md             → MUST have frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, version)
395: ├─> Command              → MUST have frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
396: ├─> Skill Reference/Asset → MUST have the 5-field block (title, description,
397: │                           trigger_phrases, importance_tier, contextType)
398: ├─> Knowledge (outside skills) → MUST NOT have frontmatter (remove if present)
399: ├─> Spec                 → SHOULD NOT have frontmatter (suggest removal)
400: └─> README               → No specific requirement (usually none)
401: ```
402: 
403: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Validation Logic
404: 
405: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
406: ```markdown
407: Validate the document structure:
408: 1. Check if required sections exist
409: 2. Verify section ordering is correct
410: 3. Ensure frontmatter is valid (if present)
411: ```
412: 
413: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
414: ```python
415: def validate_document(doc, doc_type):
416:     """Validate document structure and content"""
417: 
418:     errors = []
419: 
420:     # Check required sections
421:     required_sections = get_required_sections(doc_type)
422:     for section in required_sections:
423:         if section not in doc.sections:
424:             errors.append(f"Missing required section: {section}")
425: 
426:     # Verify section ordering
427:     expected_order = get_section_order(doc_type)
428:     actual_order = [s.name for s in doc.sections]
429:     if actual_order != expected_order:
430:         errors.append(f"Section order incorrect. Expected: {expected_order}")
431: 
432:     # Validate frontmatter
433:     if doc.has_frontmatter:
434:         frontmatter_errors = validate_frontmatter(doc.frontmatter, doc_type)
435:         errors.extend(frontmatter_errors)
436: 
437:     return errors
438: ```
439: 
440: ---
441: 
442: ## 7. WORKFLOW PATTERNS
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Show how to represent multi-step workflows using YAML structures.
445: 
446: ### YAML Pipeline: Document Creation Workflow
447: 
448: **Before (Markdown List)**:
449: ```markdown
450: 1. Analyze the request and determine document type
451: 2. Select appropriate template
452: 3. Populate template with content
453: 4. Validate structure and content
454: 5. Apply formatting standards
455: 6. Run quality checks
456: ```
457: 
458: **After (YAML Pipeline)**:
459: ```yaml
460: document_creation_workflow:
461:   phase_1_analysis:
462:     action: "Analyze request and determine document type"
463:     output: "Document type classification"
464:     validation: "Type must be one of: SKILL, Command, Knowledge, Spec, README"
465: 
466:   phase_2_template_selection:
467:     action: "Select appropriate template based on document type"
468:     output: "Template file path"
469:     depends_on: "phase_1_analysis"
470: 
471:   phase_3_population:
472:     action: "Populate template with user-provided content"
473:     output: "Draft document with filled sections"
474:     depends_on: "phase_2_template_selection"
475: 
476:   phase_4_validation:
477:     action: "Validate structure, frontmatter, section ordering"
478:     output: "Validation report (errors/warnings)"
479:     depends_on: "phase_3_population"
480: 
481:   phase_5_formatting:
482:     action: "Apply code standards (spacing, headers)"
483:     output: "Formatted document"
484:     depends_on: "phase_4_validation"
485: 
486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"
490: ```
491: 
492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags
493: 
494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:
495: ```markdown
496: | Feature           | Default | Description                         |
497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
498: | strict_validation | true    | Enforce all validation rules        |
499: | auto_fix          | false   | Automatically fix formatting issues |
500: | frontmatter_check | true    | Validate frontmatter per document type |
501: ```
502: 
503: **After (YAML Configuration)**:
504: ```yaml
505: feature_flags:
506:   strict_validation:
507:     default: true
508:     description: "Enforce all validation rules without warnings"
509:     values: [true, false]
510: 
511:   auto_fix:
512:     default: false
513:     description: "Automatically fix formatting issues during validation"
514:     values: [true, false]
515:     warning: "Use with caution - may change document semantics"
516: 
517:   frontmatter_check:
518:     default: true
519:     description: "Validate frontmatter fields per document type"
520:     values: [true, false]
521:     enforcement_level: "error"
522: ```
523: 
524: ### YAML Workflow: Multi-Branch Decision Process
525: 
526: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
527: ```markdown
528: The system should detect when to generate variants:
529: - If user explicitly requests options (shows me options, variations, different approaches)
530: - If complexity is high (7+) and uncertainty signals are present (not sure, what would work)
531: - Otherwise, generate single solution
532: 
533: Variant count depends on complexity:
534: - Simple: 2-3 variants
535: - Standard: 3-5 variants
536: - Complex: 5-10 variants
537: ```
538: 
539: **After (YAML Multi-Branch)**:
540: ```yaml
541: variant_generation_logic:
542:   triggers:
543:     explicit:
544:       keywords: ["show me options", "variations", "different approaches", "multiple designs"]
545:       action: "Generate variants immediately"
546:       priority: "high"
547: 
548:     implicit:
549:       conditions:
550:         - "complexity >= 7"
551:         - "uncertainty_signals present"
552:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work", "best approach"]
553:       action: "Generate variants with uncertainty disclaimer"
554:       priority: "medium"
555: 
556:     default:
557:       action: "Generate single optimal solution"
558:       priority: "low"
559: 
560:   variant_count_guidelines:
561:     simple:
562:       complexity_range: [1, 3]
563:       variant_count: "2-3"
564: 
565:     standard:
566:       complexity_range: [4, 6]
567:       variant_count: "3-5"
568: 
569:     complex:
570:       complexity_range: [7, 10]
571:       variant_count: "5-10"
572: 
573:     user_specified:
574:       action: "Honor user's requested count"
575:       override: true
576: ```

580: ## 8. CONFIGURATION TEMPLATES
581: 
582: **Purpose**: Demonstrate structured data formats for configuration and metadata.
583: 
584: ### YAML: Tool Configuration
585: 
586: ```yaml

603:     output:

605:       verbosity: "normal"     # minimal | normal | verbose

675: ## 9. TEMPLATE GUIDELINES
676: 
677: ### Naming Conventions
678: 
679: **File Names** (kebab-case required):
680: - Format: `[topic]-[type].md`
681: - Use hyphens, not underscores
682: - Lowercase only
683: - Descriptive and specific
684: - Examples:
685:   - ✅ `frontmatter-templates.md`
686:   - ✅ `validation-reference.md`
687:   - ✅ `config-examples.yaml`
688:   - ✅ `packaging-guide.md`
689:   - ❌ `templates.md` (too generic)
690:   - ❌ `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (wrong case)
691:   - ❌ `frontmatter_templates.md` (underscores are not canonical)
692: 
693: **Type-Specific Patterns**:
694: 
695: | Asset Type | Naming Pattern           | Kebab-case Examples          |
696: | ---------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
697: | Template   | `[content]-templates.md` | `frontmatter-templates.md`   |
698: | Reference  | `[topic]-reference.md`   | `emoji-reference.md`         |
699: | Example    | `[topic]-examples.md`    | `optimization-examples.md`   |
700: | Guide      | `[process]-guide.md`     | `packaging-guide.md`         |
701: | Checklist  | `[topic]-checklist.md`   | `validation-checklist.md`    |
702: 
703: **Section Names**:
704: - Use title case
705: - Be descriptive but concise
706: - Number if sequential: `1. Template Name`
707: 
708: ### Content Organization
709: 
710: **Progressive Disclosure**:
711: 1. **Introduction**: What this is, why it exists (1-2 sentences)
712: 2. **Sections**: Each covers one topic completely
713: 3. **Examples**: Show, don't just tell
714: 4. **Quick Reference**: Summary at end (optional)
715: 
716: **Section Structure**:
717: - **Purpose**: Why this section exists
718: - **Guidelines**: How to use the content
719: - **Template**: Copy-paste starting point
720: - **Example**: Complete working example
721: 
722: ### Formatting Standards
723: 
724: **Code Blocks**:
725: - Always specify language: ` ```yaml `, ` ```markdown `, ` ```bash `
726: - Include comments explaining non-obvious parts
727: - Show complete, runnable examples
728: - Use placeholder values that are obviously placeholders
729: 
730: **Placeholders**:
731: - Format: `[descriptive-name]` or `your-value-here`
732: - Examples:
733:   - ✅ `[skill-name]`, `[feature-description]`, `your-project-name`
734:   - ❌ `xxx`, `placeholder`, `FIXME`
735: 
736: **Lists**:
737: - Use `-` for unordered lists
738: - Use `1.` for ordered lists
739: - Nested lists indent by 2 spaces
740: - Keep items parallel in structure
741: 
742: **Tables**:
743: - Include header row
744: - Align consistently (usually left-aligned)
745: - Keep rows concise (1-2 lines)
746: - Use for comparisons or reference data
747: 
748: ### Writing Style
749: 
750: **Clarity**:
751: - Write for someone unfamiliar with your skill
752: - Define domain-specific terms on first use
753: - Use active voice: "Create the file" not "The file should be created"
754: - Be concise but complete
755: 
756: **Examples**:
757: - Every template should have a complete example

770: ## 10. ASSET FILE CHECKLIST
771: 
772: **Before creating an asset file, verify**:
773: 
774: ```markdown

776: □ Title with descriptive subtitle

797: □ File size appropriate (typically 100-800 lines)
798: □ Content is self-contained (doesn't require external context)
799: ```

855: ## 12. ASSET MAINTENANCE
856: 
857: ### When to Update Assets
858: 
859: **Update asset files when**:
860: - New template variations emerge
861: - User feedback reveals confusion
862: - Standards or conventions change
863: - New use cases discovered

866: **Version control**:

872: ### Deprecation Strategy
873:

875: 1. Mark as deprecated in section header: `## DEPRECATED: Template Name`

14: # Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines
15: 
16: Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### When to Create Assets
21: 
22: **Create an asset file when:**
23: - Templates users apply repeatedly
24: - Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
25: - Multiple examples of same pattern exist
26: - Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
27: - Template variations for different scenarios
28: 
29: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
30: - Content <30 lines
31: - Tightly coupled to workflow logic
32: - Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
33: - Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)
34: 
35: ### Location & Naming
36: 
37: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`
38: 
39: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension
40: 
41: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
42: |---------------|-----------------|
43: | `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
44: | `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
45: | `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
46: | `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES
51: 
52: ### Template Files
53: **Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks
54: 
55: **Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
56: - Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`
57: 
58: **Structure**:
59: - One template per section
60: - Include field descriptions
61: - Show complete examples
62: - Explain when to use each template
63: 
64: **Use cases**:
65: - Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
66: - Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
67: - Code templates (functions, classes, modules)
68: 
69: ### Reference Files
70: **Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data
71: 
72: **Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
73: - Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`
74: 
75: **Structure**:
76: - Tables or lists for quick lookup
77: - Decision matrices
78: - Classification systems
79: - Standards and conventions
80: 
81: **Use cases**:
82: - Emoji selection guides
83: - File type classifications
84: - Validation rule sets
85: - Naming conventions
86: 
87: ### Example Files
88: **Purpose**: Show working examples of skill outputs
89: 
90: **Naming**: `[topic]-examples.md`
91: - Example: `optimization-examples.md`, `skill-examples.md`
92: 
93: **Structure**:
94: - Before/after comparisons
95: - Annotated examples
96: - Multiple variations
97: - Anti-patterns to avoid
98: 
99: **Use cases**:
100: - Complete skill applications
101: - Common patterns
102: - Edge cases
103: - Quality standards
104: 
105: ### Guide Files
106: **Purpose**: Detailed how-to guides for complex processes
107: 
108: **Naming**: `[process]-guide.md`
109: - Example: `packaging-guide.md`, `distribution-guide.md`
110: 
111: **Structure**:
112: - Step-by-step instructions
113: - Troubleshooting sections
114: - Best practices
115: - Common pitfalls
116: 
117: **Use cases**:
118: - Multi-step processes
119: - Advanced techniques
120: - Workflow deep-dives
121: - Integration guides
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
126: 
127: ### Title and Intro
128: 
129: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
130: 
131: ```markdown
132: ---
133: title: [Title]
134: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
135: trigger_phrases:
136:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
137:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
138:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
139: importance_tier: normal
140: contextType: general
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: 
144: # [Title]
145: 
146: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
147: 
148: \## 1. OVERVIEW
149: 
150: ### Purpose
151: 
152: [Why this asset exists]
153: 
154: ### Usage
155: 
156: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: \## 2. [Content Section]
161: 
162: [The actual template/checklist/snippet content]
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## N. Related Resources (optional, if present must be last)
167: 
168: [Links to related files]
169: 
170: ```
171: 
172: Every asset file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content, `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, and `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
173: 
174: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and OVERVIEW section.**
175: > The intro is a hook. OVERVIEW provides the details.
176: 
177: #### GOOD Intro Structure
178: 
179: ```markdown
180: # Git Commit Templates
181: 
182: Copy the template that matches the change, fill the fields, and commit.
183: 
184: \## 1. OVERVIEW
185: 
186: ### Purpose
187: 
188: Uniform messages let a reader scan history by intent instead of by author.
189: 
190: ### Usage
191: 
192: Copy the appropriate template based on commit type...
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: \## 2. COMMIT TEMPLATES
197: ...
198: ```
199: 
200: #### BAD Intro Structure (too long, has subsections)
201: 
202: ```markdown
203: # Git Commit Templates
204: 
205: Copy-paste templates for creating well-structured commit messages.
206: 
207: ### Core Principle    ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
208: Atomic commits with clear intent = maintainable history.
209: 
210: ### When to Use       ← WRONG: This belongs in OVERVIEW section!
211: - Creating new features
212: - Fixing bugs
213: 
214: ---
215: ```
216: 
217: ### Intro vs OVERVIEW Content Placement
218: 
219: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | OVERVIEW Section       |
220: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
221: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat)    |
222: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
223: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
224: | How to copy/customize | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
225: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
226: | Any H2/H3 subsections | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES                  |
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## 4. STANDARD ASSET STRUCTURE
231: 
232: **Template**:
233: 
234: ````markdown
235: ---
236: title: Asset Title - Descriptive Subtitle
237: description: One-line description of what this asset provides
238: trigger_phrases:
239:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
240:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
241:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
242: importance_tier: normal
243: contextType: general
244: version: 1.0.0.0
245: ---
246: 
247: # Asset Title - Descriptive Subtitle
248: 
249: Brief introduction (1-2 sentences) explaining what this asset provides and when to use it.
250: 
251: \## 1. OVERVIEW
252: 
253: ### Purpose
254: 
255: [Why this asset exists, what problem it solves]
256: 
257: ### Usage
258: 
259: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: \## 2. SECTION NAME
264: 
265: **Key Points**:
266: - Point 1
267: - Point 2
268: - Point 3
269: 
270: **Template**:
271: ```[language]
272: # Template content here
273: # With explanatory comments
274: ```
275: 
276: **Field Guidelines**:
277: 
278: **`field_name`**:
279: - Description of field
280: - Format requirements
281: - Example: `value-example`
282: 
283: **Complete Example**:
284: ```[language]
285: # Complete working example
286: # Ready to copy and adapt
287: ```
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: \## 3. SECTION NAME
292: 
293: [Continue pattern...]
294: 
295: ---
296: 
297: ## N. RELATED RESOURCES
298: 
299: [Links to related files - MUST be last section if present]
300: 
301: ````
302: 
303: ---
304: 
305: ## 5. LOGIC REPRESENTATION PATTERNS
306: 
307: **Purpose**: Guidelines for representing logic, workflows, and decision trees in asset files using structured formats instead of prose.
308: 
309: **Why Structured Logic?**
310: - **Clarity**: Executable-style logic is easier to understand than prose
311: - **AI-Friendly**: LLMs parse structured logic better than narrative descriptions
312: - **Maintainability**: Changes to logic are more visible in structured formats
313: - **Consistency**: Same patterns across all asset files
314: 
315: ### When to Use Each Format
316: 
317: **Use Python Pseudo-Code When:**
318: - Complex branching logic (multiple IF/ELIF/ELSE conditions)
319: - Function/method definitions with clear inputs/outputs
320: - State management or algorithmic processes
321: - Validation or transformation logic
322: - Examples: Mode detection, validation pipelines, decision functions
323: 
324: **Use YAML Structures When:**
325: - Configuration data (settings, options, parameters)
326: - Pipeline definitions (multi-step workflows with clear phases)
327: - Hierarchical workflows (nested processes)
328: - Metadata structures (categorization, tagging)
329: - Examples: Workflow definitions, configuration templates, feature matrices
330: 
331: **Use Markdown Decision Trees When:**
332: - Simple branching logic (2-5 branches)
333: - Visual flow representation (user-facing paths)
334: - Classification systems (type determination)
335: - Quick decision guides
336: - Examples: Document type selection, frontmatter requirements
337: 
338: **Keep Markdown Prose When:**
339: - Explanatory text and conceptual overviews
340: - Narrative examples with context
341: - Best practices guidance
342: - Introductions and summaries
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## 6. DECISION LOGIC EXAMPLES
347: 
348: **Purpose**: Demonstrate how to convert markdown prose into structured decision logic.
349: 
350: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Mode Detection
351: 
352: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
353: ```markdown
354: Check user input for mode indicators:
355: - If "$quick" is present, use quick mode with auto-scaling depth
356: - If "$ticket" is present, use ticket mode with depth 10
357: - Otherwise, use interactive mode with depth 10
358: ```
359: 
360: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
361: ```python
362: def detect_mode(request):
363:     """Detect execution mode from user request markers"""
364: 
365:     if '$quick' in request:
366:         mode = 'quick'
367:         depth = 'auto_scale_1_to_5'
368:     elif '$ticket' in request:
369:         mode = 'ticket'
370:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
371:     else:
372:         # DEFAULT TO INTERACTIVE
373:         mode = 'interactive'
374:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
375: 
376:     return mode, depth
377: ```
378: 
379: ### Markdown Decision Tree: Frontmatter Requirements
380: 
381: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
382: ```markdown
383: Different document types have different frontmatter requirements:
384: - SKILL.md files must have frontmatter with name, description, allowed-tools, and version
385: - Command files must have frontmatter with description and argument-hint
386: - Skill reference/asset files must have the 5-field block
387: - Knowledge files outside skill folders should not have frontmatter
388: - Spec files typically don't have frontmatter
389: ```
390: 
391: **After (Markdown Decision Tree)**:
392: ```
393: Document type?
394: ├─> SKILL.md             → MUST have frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, version)
395: ├─> Command              → MUST have frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
396: ├─> Skill Reference/Asset → MUST have the 5-field block (title, description,
397: │                           trigger_phrases, importance_tier, contextType)
398: ├─> Knowledge (outside skills) → MUST NOT have frontmatter (remove if present)
399: ├─> Spec                 → SHOULD NOT have frontmatter (suggest removal)
400: └─> README               → No specific requirement (usually none)
401: ```
402: 
403: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Validation Logic
404: 
405: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
406: ```markdown
407: Validate the document structure:
408: 1. Check if required sections exist
409: 2. Verify section ordering is correct
410: 3. Ensure frontmatter is valid (if present)
411: ```
412: 
413: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
414: ```python
415: def validate_document(doc, doc_type):
416:     """Validate document structure and content"""
417: 
418:     errors = []
419: 
420:     # Check required sections
421:     required_sections = get_required_sections(doc_type)
422:     for section in required_sections:
423:         if section not in doc.sections:
424:             errors.append(f"Missing required section: {section}")
425: 
426:     # Verify section ordering
427:     expected_order = get_section_order(doc_type)
428:     actual_order = [s.name for s in doc.sections]
429:     if actual_order != expected_order:
430:         errors.append(f"Section order incorrect. Expected: {expected_order}")
431: 
432:     # Validate frontmatter
433:     if doc.has_frontmatter:
434:         frontmatter_errors = validate_frontmatter(doc.frontmatter, doc_type)
435:         errors.extend(frontmatter_errors)
436: 
437:     return errors
438: ```
439: 
440: ---
441: 
442: ## 7. WORKFLOW PATTERNS
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Show how to represent multi-step workflows using YAML structures.
445: 
446: ### YAML Pipeline: Document Creation Workflow
447: 
448: **Before (Markdown List)**:
449: ```markdown
450: 1. Analyze the request and determine document type
451: 2. Select appropriate template
452: 3. Populate template with content
453: 4. Validate structure and content
454: 5. Apply formatting standards
455: 6. Run quality checks
456: ```
457: 
458: **After (YAML Pipeline)**:
459: ```yaml
460: document_creation_workflow:
461:   phase_1_analysis:
462:     action: "Analyze request and determine document type"
463:     output: "Document type classification"
464:     validation: "Type must be one of: SKILL, Command, Knowledge, Spec, README"
465: 
466:   phase_2_template_selection:
467:     action: "Select appropriate template based on document type"
468:     output: "Template file path"
469:     depends_on: "phase_1_analysis"
470: 
471:   phase_3_population:
472:     action: "Populate template with user-provided content"
473:     output: "Draft document with filled sections"
474:     depends_on: "phase_2_template_selection"
475: 
476:   phase_4_validation:
477:     action: "Validate structure, frontmatter, section ordering"
478:     output: "Validation report (errors/warnings)"
479:     depends_on: "phase_3_population"
480: 
481:   phase_5_formatting:
482:     action: "Apply code standards (spacing, headers)"
483:     output: "Formatted document"
484:     depends_on: "phase_4_validation"
485: 
486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"
490: ```
491: 
492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags
493: 
494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:
495: ```markdown
496: | Feature           | Default | Description                         |
497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
498: | strict_validation | true    | Enforce all validation rules        |
499: | auto_fix          | false   | Automatically fix formatting issues |
500: | frontmatter_check | true    | Validate frontmatter per document type |
501: ```
502: 
503: **After (YAML Configuration)**:
504: ```yaml
505: feature_flags:
506:   strict_validation:
507:     default: true
508:     description: "Enforce all validation rules without warnings"
509:     values: [true, false]
510: 
511:   auto_fix:
512:     default: false
513:     description: "Automatically fix formatting issues during validation"
514:     values: [true, false]
515:     warning: "Use with caution - may change document semantics"
516: 
517:   frontmatter_check:
518:     default: true
519:     description: "Validate frontmatter fields per document type"
520:     values: [true, false]
521:     enforcement_level: "error"
522: ```
523: 
524: ### YAML Workflow: Multi-Branch Decision Process
525: 
526: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
527: ```markdown
528: The system should detect when to generate variants:
529: - If user explicitly requests options (shows me options, variations, different approaches)
530: - If complexity is high (7+) and uncertainty signals are present (not sure, what would work)
531: - Otherwise, generate single solution
532: 
533: Variant count depends on complexity:
534: - Simple: 2-3 variants
535: - Standard: 3-5 variants
536: - Complex: 5-10 variants
537: ```
538: 
539: **After (YAML Multi-Branch)**:
540: ```yaml
541: variant_generation_logic:
542:   triggers:
543:     explicit:
544:       keywords: ["show me options", "variations", "different approaches", "multiple designs"]
545:       action: "Generate variants immediately"
546:       priority: "high"
547: 
548:     implicit:
549:       conditions:
550:         - "complexity >= 7"
551:         - "uncertainty_signals present"
552:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work", "best approach"]
553:       action: "Generate variants with uncertainty disclaimer"
554:       priority: "medium"
555: 
556:     default:
557:       action: "Generate single optimal solution"
558:       priority: "low"
559:

70: ### Title and Intro
71: 
72: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
73: 
74: ```markdown
75: ---
76: title: [Title]
77: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
78: trigger_phrases:

80:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
81:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"

685: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
686: 
687: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
688: 
689: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
690: 
691: **Decision Criteria**:
692: 
693: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
694: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
695: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
696: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
697: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
698: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
699: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
700: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
701: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
702: 
703: ### Extraction Pattern
704: 
705: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
706: ```markdown
707: ### [Workflow Name]
708: 
709: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
710: 
711: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
712: 
713: **Quick Overview**:
714: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
715: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
716: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
717: 
718: **Configuration Options:**
719: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
720: - Default values optimized for common use cases
721: ```
722: 
723: ### Benefits of Separation
724: 
725: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
726: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
727: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
728: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
729: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
730: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
731: 
732: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
733: 
734: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
735: \```python
736: def detect_mode(request):
737:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
738:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
739:     return 'interactive', 10
740: \```
741: 
742: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
743: 
744: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
745: \```python
746: from dataclasses import dataclass
747: 
748: @dataclass
749: class ModeConfig:
750:     mode: str
751:     depth_rounds: int
752: 
753: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
754:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
755:     if '$quick' in request:
756:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
757:     elif '$ticket' in request:
758:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
759:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
760: \```
761: 
762: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
763: \```python
764: def test_quick_mode():
765:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
766: \```
767: 
768: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
769:

772: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
773: 
774: ### Purpose
775: 
776: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
777: 
778: **When to use YAML**:
779: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
780: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
781: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
782: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
783: - Validation schemas
784: 
785: ### Standard YAML Structure
786: 
787: ```yaml
788: # [config-name].yaml
789: metadata:
790:   version: "1.0.0"
791:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
792: 
793: config:
794:   threshold_values:
795:     low: 1
796:     medium: 5
797:     high: 10
798:   feature_flags:
799:     enable_feature_x: true
800:   mappings:
801:     $quick: "quick_mode"
802:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
803: ```
804: 
805: ### File Organization
806: 
807: ```
808: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
809: ├── assets/
810: │   ├── workflow-configs/
811: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
812: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
813: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
814: │   ├── mappings/
815: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
816: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
817: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
818: │   └── templates/
819: │       └── [template files]
820: ```
821: 
822: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
823: 
824: ```python
825: import yaml
826: from pathlib import Path
827: 
828: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
829:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
830:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
831:     with open(config_path) as f:
832:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
833: 
834: # Usage
835: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
836: ```
837: 
838: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
839: 
840: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
841: ```markdown
842: | Trigger                    | Action             |
843: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
844: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
845: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
846: ```
847: 
848: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
849: 
850: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
851: ```yaml
852: config:
853:   variant_triggers:
854:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
855:     implicit:
856:       complexity_threshold: 7
857:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
858:   variant_count:
859:     simple: [2, 3]
860:     complex: [5, 10]
861: ```
862: 
863: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
864: ```python
865: import yaml
866: 
867: class VariantDetector:
868:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
869:         with open(config_path) as f:
870:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
871: 
872:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
873:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
874:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
875:             return True
876: 
877:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
878:         if complexity >= threshold:
879:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
880:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
881:         return False
882: ```
883: 
884: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
885:

888: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
889: 
890: ### When to Use Python for Logic
891: 
892: **Use Python scripts when**:
893: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
894: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
895: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
896: - API integration (external services)
897: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
898: 
899: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
900: 
901: **Always include**:
902: - Type hints for parameters and return values
903: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
904: - Dataclasses for structured data
905: 
906: **Example**:
907: ```python
908: from dataclasses import dataclass
909: from pathlib import Path
910: 
911: @dataclass
912: class ValidationResult:
913:     is_valid: bool
914:     errors: list[str]
915: 
916: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
917:     """
918:     Validate configuration file.
919: 
920:     Args:
921:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
922: 
923:     Returns:
924:         ValidationResult with status and errors
925: 
926:     Raises:
927:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
928:     """
929:     if not config_path.exists():
930:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
931:     # Validation logic
932:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
933: ```
934: 
935: ### Unit Testing Requirements
936: 
937: **Every Python script must have tests**:
938: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
939: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
940: - Framework: pytest
941: 
942: **Example**:
943: ```python
944: import pytest
945: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
946: 
947: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
948:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
949:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
950:     result = validate_config(config)
951:     assert result.is_valid
952: 
953: def test_validate_missing_file():
954:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
955:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
956: ```
957: 
958: ### Import and Reference Patterns
959: 
960: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
961: 
962: **Markdown references**:
963: ```markdown
964: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
965: ```
966: 
967: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
968: 
969: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
970: ```markdown
971: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
972: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
973: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
974: ```
975: 
976: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
977: 
978: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
979: ```python
980: from typing import Literal
981: from dataclasses import dataclass
982: 
983: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
984: 
985: @dataclass
986: class WorkflowDecision:
987:     mode: WorkflowMode
988:     depth_rounds: int
989: 
990: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
991:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
992:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
993:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
994:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
995:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
996:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
997: ```
998: 
999: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
1000: ```python
1001: def test_quick_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1003: 
1004: def test_default_mode():
1005:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1006: ```
1007: 
1008: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1009:

1012: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1013: 
1014: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1015: 
1016: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1017: 
1018: ```
1019: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1020: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1021: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1022: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1023: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1024: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1025: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1026: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1027: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1028: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1029: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1030: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1031: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1032: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1033: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1034: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1035: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1036: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1037: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1038: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1039: │       ├── template-name.md
1040: │       └── component-template.tsx
1041: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1042:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1043:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1044:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1045:     └── __init__.py
1046: ```
1047: 
1048: ### Directory Purposes
1049: 
1050: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1051: 
1052: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1053: 
1054: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1055: 
1056: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1057: 
1058: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1059: 
1060: ### When to Create Each Directory
1061: 
1062: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1063: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1064: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1065: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1066: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
23: 
24: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
25: 
26: **Core Purpose**:
27: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
28: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
29: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
30: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
31: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
32: 
33: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
34: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
35: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
36: 
37: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
38: 
39: ```
40: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
41:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
42:             ↓
43: Level 2: SKILL.md body
44:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
45:             ↓
46: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
47:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
48: ```
49: 
50: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
51: 
52: ### Location & Naming
53: 
54: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
55: 
56: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
57: 
58: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
59: |---------------|-----------------|
60: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
61: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
62: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
63: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
64: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
69: 
70: ### Title and Intro
71: 
72: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
73: 
74: ```markdown
75: ---
76: title: [Title]
77: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
78: trigger_phrases:
79:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
80:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
81:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
82: importance_tier: normal
83: contextType: general
84: version: 1.0.0.0
85: ---
86: 
87: # [Title]
88: 
89: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: \## 1. OVERVIEW
94: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
95: 
96: ```
97: 
98: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block. The Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal:
99: - 3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content
100: - `importance_tier`, which defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs
101: - `contextType`, one of `planning|research|implementation|general`
102: 
103: See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
104: 
105: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
106: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
107: 
108: #### GOOD Intro Structure
109: 
110: ```markdown
111: # Git Commit Workflows
112: 
113: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: \## 1. OVERVIEW
118: 
119: ### Purpose
120: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
121: 
122: ### When to Use
123: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
124: - Filtering generated files from commits
125: - Writing clear commit messages
126: 
127: ### Core Principle
128: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
129: ```
130: 
131: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
132: 
133: ```markdown
134: # Git Commit Workflows
135: 
136: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
137: 
138: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
139: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
140: 
141: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
142: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: \## 1. OVERVIEW
147: 
148: ### Purpose
149: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
150: 
151: ### Core Principle
152: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
153: ```
154: 
155: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
156: 
157: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
158: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
159: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
160: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
161: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
162: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
163: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
164: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
165: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ### Reference Body Skeleton
170: 
171: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
172: 
173: ```markdown
174: # [Title]
175: 
176: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 1. OVERVIEW
181: 
182: ### Purpose
183: 
184: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
185: 
186: ### When to Use
187: 
188: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
189: - [Second trigger]
190: 
191: ### Core Principle
192: 
193: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
194: 
195: ### Boundaries
196: 
197: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
198: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
199: 
200: ### Key Sources
201: 
202: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
203: 
204: ---
205: 
206: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
207: 
208: ### [Rule Group]
209: 
210: - **Rule:** [What to do]
211: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
212: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
217: 
218: [Body of the section]
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
223: 
224: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
225: ```
226: 
227: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
228: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
229: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
230: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
231: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
232: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
233: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
234: 
235: ---
236: 
237: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
238: 
239: ### Create Reference File When
240: 
241: **Workflow Complexity**:
242: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
243: - Decision trees with multiple branches
244: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
245: - Systematic debugging procedures
246: 
247: **Technical Depth**:
248: - Root cause analysis required
249: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
250: - Before/after code transformations
251: - Common error patterns and fixes
252: 
253: **Size Threshold**:
254: - Content exceeds 200 lines
255: - Multiple related workflows
256: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
257: 
258: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
259: 
260: **Core Content**:
261: - Overview and "When to Use"
262: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
263: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
264:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
265: - Quick reference
266: 
267: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
268: 
269: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
270: 
271: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
272: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
273: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
274: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
275: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
276: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
277: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
278: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
279: 
280: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
281: 
282: ---
283: 
284: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
285: 
286: ### Core Principle Statements
287: 
288: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
289: 
290: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
291: 
292: **Format**:
293: ```markdown
294: \## 1. OVERVIEW
295: 
296: ### Purpose
297: 
298: [The outcome this reference produces]
299: 
300: ### When to Use
301: 
302: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
303: 
304: ### Core Principle
305: 
306: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
307: ```
308: 
309: **Examples from Real Skills**:
310: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
311: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
312: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
313: 
314: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
315: 
316: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
317: 
318: **Format**:
319: ```markdown
320: ### The [Number] Phases
321: 
322: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
323: 
324: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
325: 
326: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
327: 
328: **Actions**:
329: 1. [Action 1]
330: 2. [Action 2]
331: 
332: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
333: 
334: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
335: 
336: [Similar structure]
337: ```
338: 
339: **Key Elements**:
340: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
341: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
342: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
343: 
344: ### Before/After Code Examples
345: 
346: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
347: 
348: **Format**:
349: ```markdown
350: ### [Pattern Name]
351: 
352: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
353: \```[language]
354: // Bad code with issues
355: // Showing what NOT to do
356: \```
357: 
358: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
359: \```[language]
360: // Good code with fixes
361: // Showing correct approach
362: \```
363: 
364: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
365: ```
366: 
367: **Key Elements**:
368: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
369: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
370: - Inline comments explaining issues
371: - "Why better" rationale
372: 
373: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
374: 
375: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
376: 
377: **Format**:
378: ```markdown
379: ### Common Patterns
380: 
381: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
382: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
383: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
384: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
385: ```
386: 
387: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
388: 
389: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
390: 
391: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
392: 
393: **Format**:
394: \```markdown
395: ### Decision Logic
396: 
397: \```markdown
398: IF [condition A]:
399:   → [Action/Path A]
400:   → [Expected outcome A]
401: 
402: IF [condition B]:
403:   → [Action/Path B]
404:   → [Expected outcome B]
405: 
406: IF [condition C]:
407:   → [Action/Path C]
408:   → [Expected outcome C]
409: \```
410: \```
411: 
412: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
413: \```markdown
414: \```
415: Analyze situation
416: ├─ Condition A met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
418: │     └─ Expected outcome A
419: ├─ Condition B met
420: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
421: │     └─ Expected outcome B
422: └─ Condition C met
423:    └─ Execute Workflow C
424:       └─ Expected outcome C
425: \```
426: \```
427: 
428: ### Validation Checkpoints
429: 
430: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
431: 
432: **Format**:
433: ```markdown
434: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
435: ```
436: 
437: **Examples**:
438: - `files_analyzed`
439: - `artifacts_filtered`
440: - `strategy_determined`
441: - `root_cause_identified`
442: 
443: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
444: 
445: ### Prerequisites Section
446: 
447: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
448: 
449: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.

451: **Format**:
452: ```markdown
453: # [Workflow Name]
454: 
455: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
456:

460:

466: ```
467: 
468: **Key Elements**:
469: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
470: - Links to other reference files
471: - Lists specific requirements
472: 
473: ### Tool Integration References
474: 
475: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
476: 
477: **Format for MCP Tools**:
478: \```markdown
479: **Automated [Task] via MCP:**
480: 
481: Instead of [manual approach], use Chrome DevTools MCP:
482: 
483: \```markdown
484: 1. [Step 1]:
485:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
486:    - parameter1: "value"
487:    - parameter2: value
488: 
489: 2. [Step 2]:

491: \```
492: 
493: **What you'll see:**
494: - [Expected output 1]
495: - [Expected output 2]
496: 
497: **Example output:**
498: \```json

500:   "field": "value",
501:   "data": "example"
502: }
503: \```
504: \```
505: 
506: **Format for Scripts**:
507: ```markdown

509: ```
510: 
511: **Format for Assets**:
512: ```markdown

514: ```
515: 
516: ### Common Error Patterns
517: 
518: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
519: 
520: **Format**:
521: \```markdown

523: 
524: \```javascript

526: // → [What it means]

529: // [Another error message]
530: // → [What it means]
531: // → [How to fix]

533: \```
534: 
535: **Example**:

537: **Common Browser Errors:**
538: 
539: \```javascript
540: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
541: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
542: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
543: 
544: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
545: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource
546: // → Check Network tab, test with extensions disabled

548: \```

551: 
552: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope
553: 
554: **Format**:
555: ```markdown

557: 
558: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]

684: 
685: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
686: 
687: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
688: 
689: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
690: 
691: **Decision Criteria**:
692: 
693: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
694: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
695: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
696: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
697: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
698: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
699: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
700: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
701: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
702: 
703: ### Extraction Pattern
704: 
705: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
706: ```markdown
707: ### [Workflow Name]
708: 
709: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
710: 
711: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
712: 
713: **Quick Overview**:
714: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
715: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
716: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
717: 
718: **Configuration Options:**
719: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
720: - Default values optimized for common use cases
721: ```
722: 
723: ### Benefits of Separation
724: 
725: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
726: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
727: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
728: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
729: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
730: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
731: 
732: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
733: 
734: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
735: \```python
736: def detect_mode(request):
737:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
738:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
739:     return 'interactive', 10
740: \```

751:     depth_rounds: int
752:

754:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""

757:     elif '$ticket' in request:

768: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

772: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
773: 
774: ### Purpose
775: 
776: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
777: 
778: **When to use YAML**:
779: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
780: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
781: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
782: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
783: - Validation schemas
784: 
785: ### Standard YAML Structure
786: 
787: ```yaml
788: # [config-name].yaml
789: metadata:
790:   version: "1.0.0"
791:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
792: 
793: config:
794:   threshold_values:
795:     low: 1
796:     medium: 5
797:     high: 10
798:   feature_flags:
799:     enable_feature_x: true
800:   mappings:
801:     $quick: "quick_mode"
802:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
803: ```
804: 
805: ### File Organization
806: 
807: ```
808: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
809: ├── assets/
810: │   ├── workflow-configs/
811: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
812: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
813: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
814: │   ├── mappings/
815: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
816: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
817: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
818: │   └── templates/
819: │       └── [template files]
820: ```
821: 
822: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
823: 
824: ```python
825: import yaml
826: from pathlib import Path
827: 
828: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
829:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
830:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
831:     with open(config_path) as f:
832:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
833: 
834: # Usage
835: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
836: ```
837: 
838: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
839: 
840: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
841: ```markdown
842: | Trigger                    | Action             |
843: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
844: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
845: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
846: ```
847: 
848: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
849: 
850: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
851: ```yaml
852: config:
853:   variant_triggers:
854:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
855:     implicit:
856:       complexity_threshold: 7
857:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
858:   variant_count:
859:     simple: [2, 3]
860:     complex: [5, 10]
861: ```
862: 
863: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
864: ```python
865: import yaml
866: 
867: class VariantDetector:
868:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
869:         with open(config_path) as f:
870:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
871: 
872:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
873:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
874:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
875:             return True
876: 
877:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
878:         if complexity >= threshold:
879:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
880:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
881:         return False
882: ```
883: 
884: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

886: ---

888: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
889: 
890: ### When to Use Python for Logic
891: 
892: **Use Python scripts when**:
893: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
894: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
895: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
896: - API integration (external services)
897: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
898: 
899: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
900: 
901: **Always include**:
902: - Type hints for parameters and return values
903: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
904: - Dataclasses for structured data
905: 
906: **Example**:
907: ```python
908: from dataclasses import dataclass
909: from pathlib import Path
910: 
911: @dataclass
912: class ValidationResult:
913:     is_valid: bool
914:     errors: list[str]
915: 
916: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
917:     """
918:     Validate configuration file.
919: 
920:     Args:
921:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
922: 
923:     Returns:
924:         ValidationResult with status and errors
925: 
926:     Raises:
927:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
928:     """
929:     if not config_path.exists():
930:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
931:     # Validation logic
932:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
933: ```
934: 
935: ### Unit Testing Requirements
936: 
937: **Every Python script must have tests**:
938: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
939: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
940: - Framework: pytest
941: 
942: **Example**:
943: ```python
944: import pytest
945: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
946: 
947: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
948:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
949:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
950:     result = validate_config(config)
951:     assert result.is_valid
952: 
953: def test_validate_missing_file():
954:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
955:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
956: ```
957: 
958: ### Import and Reference Patterns
959: 
960: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
961: 
962: **Markdown references**:
963: ```markdown
964: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
965: ```
966: 
967: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
968: 
969: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
970: ```markdown
971: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
972: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
973: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
974: ```
975: 
976: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
977: 
978: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
979: ```python
980: from typing import Literal
981: from dataclasses import dataclass
982: 
983: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
984: 
985: @dataclass
986: class WorkflowDecision:
987:     mode: WorkflowMode
988:     depth_rounds: int
989: 
990: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
991:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
992:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
993:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
994:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
995:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
996:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
997: ```
998: 
999: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
1000: ```python

1002:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1003: 
1004: def test_default_mode():
1005:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1006: ```
1007: 
1008: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1009:
